recipes.name: Skillet Beef & Broccoli
recipes.desc: Beef strips, crisp broccoli, garlic-ginger sauce over steamed jasmine rice
recipe: Toss beef with cornstarch, soy sauce, sesame oil. Marinate 5 min.
Heat oil in large skillet on high. Sear beef 2-3 min. Remove.
Add broccoli, garlic, ginger. Stir fry 3 min.
Return beef, toss 1 min. Serve over steamed jasmine rice.
recipes.tip: Slice the beef paper-thin against the grain and freeze for 15 minutes first - it cuts much easier and stays tender under high heat.
recipes.tip2: The key to stir-fry is not moving things. Let the beef sit untouched for 60 seconds before tossing — that contact with the hot pan builds the caramelized crust.
recipe_detailed: If the beef isn't already sliced, place it in the freezer for 15 min — it firms up and slices much thinner. Cut across the grain (perpendicular to the muscle fibers) into strips about ¼-inch thick. Thin slices mean fast searing and tender results.
In a bowl, toss the beef with cornstarch, soy sauce, and sesame oil. The cornstarch forms a light crust and helps thicken the sauce later. Let it sit 5 min while you prep everything else.

Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat until very hot — a drop of water should evaporate immediately. Add oil, then the beef in a single layer. Don't crowd the pan or it steams instead of sears. Cook 60 seconds without touching, then toss once more for 30 seconds. Remove to a plate — it'll finish cooking when you return it.
Add broccoli, garlic, and ginger to the same pan. Stir fry 3 min — the broccoli should be bright green and just tender but still have a snap.
Return the beef to the pan and add any sauce. Toss everything together for 1 min until the sauce thickens and coats the beef. Serve immediately over steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.name: Taco Bowl
recipes.desc: Seasoned ground beef, black beans, pico, avocado, romaine
recipe: Brown ground beef, drain fat.
Add taco seasoning + 2 tbsp water, stir 1 min.
Divide romaine into bowls. Add beef, beans, pico, avocado.
Squeeze fresh lime over everything.
recipes.tip: Toast the taco seasoning in a dry pan for 30 seconds before adding meat. The heat blooms the spices and deepens the flavor significantly.
recipes.tip2: Let the beef sit in the pan undisturbed for 30 seconds at a time — you want a browned crust, not steamed grey meat. Crowded pan means no crust.
recipe_detailed: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add onion and cook 3 min until softened. Add ground beef, breaking it into small pieces. Cook 6-8 min without stirring too often — you want browning, not grey crumbles.
Drain off excess fat, leaving a thin film. Add taco seasoning and a splash of water, stir to coat. Cook 1-2 min until the water evaporates and the spices cling to the meat.
Warm the rice and build bowls: rice first, then beef, then toppings. For guac, mash avocado with lime juice and salt — taste as you go, it should be bright and a little salty.
Top each bowl with salsa, sour cream, shredded cheese, and a squeeze of lime. Eat while the beef is hot.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Flank Steak
recipes.desc: Marinated flank steak, roasted asparagus, lemon
recipe: Preheat oven to 425°F. Mix oil, garlic, lemon zest, paprika.
Coat steak and asparagus. Place on sheet pan.
Roast 12-15 min for medium-rare. Rest steak 5 min.
Slice and serve with asparagus and lemon juice.
recipes.tip: Let the steak rest at room temperature 20 minutes before cooking. Cold meat seizes up and cooks unevenly. Resting after is equally important - don't skip it.
recipes.tip2: Slice across the grain — look for the direction the muscle fibers run, then cut perpendicular to them. Cutting with the grain gives you chewy, stringy steak. Against it: tender every time.
recipe_detailed: Preheat oven to 425F and line a sheet pan with foil. Pat the flank steak dry with paper towels — moisture prevents browning. Season all sides generously with salt, pepper, and any rub.
Toss vegetables in oil, salt, and pepper and spread on one side of the pan. Place the steak on the other side.

Roast 10-14 min depending on thickness. For medium-rare, pull it when a meat thermometer reads 130F — it will climb to 135F as it rests. Flank steak goes from perfect to tough quickly, so check early.
Rest the steak on a cutting board for at least 5 min before cutting. Slice thin against the grain and fan over the roasted vegetables.

recipes.name: Zucchini Noodle Bolognese
recipes.desc: Rich meat sauce over spiralized zucchini
recipe: Sauté onion 3 min. Add garlic 1 min.
Add beef, brown fully. Drain fat.
Add tomatoes and seasoning. Simmer 10 min.
Sauté zucchini noodles 2 min. Top with sauce, basil, parmesan.
recipes.tip: Add a parmesan rind to the tomato sauce while it simmers. Remove before serving - it adds a savory depth you can't get any other way.
recipes.tip2: Zucchini noodles release a lot of water as they cook. Toss them in the hot sauce for no more than 2 min — any longer and your sauce turns into soup.
recipe_detailed: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add onion, carrot, and celery and cook 5-7 min until softened. Add garlic, cook 1 min.
Add ground beef and cook 6-8 min, breaking into fine crumbles, until browned with no pink remaining. Drain excess fat — leave a thin layer for flavor.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, and herbs. Stir well, reduce heat to low, and simmer 20-25 min uncovered. The sauce should thicken and deepen in color.
Spiralize the zucchini into noodles. Add them to the sauce and toss gently for 1-2 min — just until warmed through. Season and serve immediately topped with Parmesan.

recipes.name: Korean Beef Bowl
recipes.desc: Tender strips of Mongolian-style beef in a sweet-savory soy-ginger glaze over jasmine rice with green onions
ingredients: 1.5 lb flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain
recipe: Toss sliced flank steak with cornstarch to coat. Shake off excess.
Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, hoisin, garlic, ginger, and red pepper flakes together.
Heat oil in wok over high heat. Sear beef in batches 1-2 min per side until caramelized. Remove and drain oil.
Return beef to pan, pour sauce over, toss 1-2 min until thickened and glossy.
Serve over jasmine rice topped with green onions and sesame seeds.
recipes.tip: Slice flank steak partially frozen for ultra-thin strips. High heat in batches gives caramelized beef, not steamed.
recipes.tip2: Sear in batches — never more than a single layer of beef in the pan. Crowding drops the pan temperature and the beef steams grey instead of caramelizing.
recipe_detailed: Slice the flank steak as thin as possible against the grain. If it is hard to slice thin, freeze for 20 min first — it firms up and cuts cleanly.
Toss sliced beef with cornstarch to coat lightly. This helps it caramelize and thickens the sauce later. Shake off any excess.
Whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, hoisin, garlic, ginger, and red pepper flakes. Taste — it should be salty-sweet with a little heat.

Heat oil in a wok or large skillet over the highest heat your stove has. Add beef in a single layer, sear 60 seconds, toss briefly and cook 30 more seconds. Remove and repeat with remaining beef. Return all beef, pour sauce over, toss 1-2 min until glossy and thickened. Serve over jasmine rice with green onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Egg Roll in a Bowl
recipes.desc: Ground beef, coleslaw mix, soy-ginger sauce
recipe: Brown beef in large skillet. Drain.
Add garlic and ginger, cook 1 min.
Add coleslaw mix, stir fry 3-4 min.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil. Toss. Top with green onion.
recipes.tip: Press the coleslaw mix gently with a paper towel before adding it to the pan to remove excess moisture. Drier cabbage browns better and soaks up the sauce.
recipes.tip2: The coleslaw mix finishes cooking in about 3 min — you want it wilted but still with a little bite, not completely collapsed. Taste a strand before pulling it off the heat.
recipe_detailed: Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high. Add garlic and ginger and stir 30 seconds until fragrant. Add ground beef and cook 6 min, breaking into crumbles, until browned.
Drain excess fat, leaving a thin layer. Push the beef to the sides. Add the coleslaw mix to the center and stir fry 2-3 min until just wilted but still slightly crisp.
Mix in soy sauce, sesame oil, and rice vinegar. Toss everything together and cook 1 more minute. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve topped with sliced green onions, sriracha, and a drizzle of sesame oil. Optionally top with a fried egg.

recipes.name: Beef & Cabbage Stir Fry
recipes.desc: Ground beef, shredded cabbage, soy-ginger sauce
recipe: Brown beef in large skillet. Drain.
Add garlic and ginger, stir 1 min.
Add cabbage, cook 3-4 min until slightly wilted.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil. Top with green onion and sesame seeds.
recipes.tip: Add a splash of rice vinegar right at the end of cooking. The acidity cuts through the richness and brightens everything without tasting sour.
recipes.tip2: Add the cabbage in batches if your pan is small — let each batch wilt slightly before adding more. Trying to fit it all at once drops the pan temp and it steams instead of stir fries.
recipe_detailed: Slice beef thin against the grain. Toss with soy sauce and a pinch of cornstarch. Set aside while you prep everything else — stir fry moves fast.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until smoking. Add oil, then beef in a single layer. Sear 60 seconds without touching, then toss for 30 seconds. Remove to a plate.
In the same pan add garlic and ginger and stir 30 seconds. Add cabbage and stir fry 3-4 min until wilted and edges begin to char slightly.
Return beef to the pan. Add sauce, toss everything together for 1 min until coated. Serve over rice with a drizzle of sesame oil.

recipes.name: Campechano Street Tacos
recipes.desc: Grilled carne asada + chorizo blend, corn tortillas, onion, cilantro, salsa verde
recipe: Season skirt steak with cumin and salt. Grill or sear on cast iron 3-4 min per side.
Cook chorizo in a separate skillet, breaking up, 5 min. Drain excess fat.
Rest steak 3 min, then chop into small pieces. Mix with chorizo.
Warm tortillas on the grill or dry skillet. Double up each taco.
Fill with meat blend. Top with onion, cilantro, squeeze of lime, salsa verde.
recipes.tip: For campechano, the chorizo fat is the sauce. Don't drain it - mix the chopped steak directly into the chorizo drippings so the meat absorbs every bit of flavor.
recipes.tip2: Double up your tortillas — street tacos always use two corn tortillas per taco. Warm them directly on a gas burner or in a dry skillet until charred in spots. The char is flavor.
recipe_detailed: If using steak, slice thin against the grain and season generously with salt, pepper, and cumin. If using chorizo, remove from casing and crumble.
Heat a cast iron or heavy skillet over high heat until very hot. Add a thin film of oil. Cook steak in batches 1-2 min per side for medium, or cook chorizo until crispy and rendered.
Warm tortillas directly over a gas flame for 20 seconds per side, or in a dry skillet. Stack two per taco and fill with the hot meat.
Top immediately with diced white onion, fresh cilantro, a squeeze of lime, and salsa. Eat while hot — corn tortillas toughen as they cool.

recipes.name: Meatloaf & Roasted Veggies
recipes.desc: Classic meatloaf with ketchup glaze, roasted green beans and carrots
ingredients: For glaze: 3 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp mustard
recipe: Preheat oven to 375°F. Mix beef, flour, eggs, milk, onion, garlic, Worcestershire, seasoning.
Form into loaf on a parchment-lined pan.
Mix ketchup, brown sugar, mustard. Spread over top.
Roast vegetables alongside with olive oil and salt.
Bake 50-55 min until internal temp reaches 160°F. Rest 10 min before slicing.
recipes.tip: Mix the meatloaf by hand just until combined. Overworking develops the gluten in the binders and results in a dense, tough loaf instead of a tender one.
recipes.tip2: Don't overmix the meatloaf. Mix just until everything is combined — overworking the meat makes it dense and tough. Use your hands and stop as soon as no dry spots remain.
recipe_detailed: Preheat oven to 375F. In a large bowl, mix ground beef, onion, garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper. Use your hands and mix only until just combined.
Shape into a loaf on a foil-lined baking sheet. Mix ketchup with a little brown sugar and brush half over the top.
Toss vegetables with oil, salt, and pepper and spread around the loaf.
Bake 45-55 min. At 30 min, brush on the rest of the glaze. The meatloaf is done when an instant-read thermometer reads 160F in the center. Let it rest 10 min before slicing.

recipes.name: Smash Burgers
recipes.desc: Crispy-edged smashed beef patties, melted cheese, lettuce wrap or bun
ingredients: 1.5 lb ground beef (80/20), formed into 6 loose balls
recipe: Heat cast iron skillet or griddle over high heat until very hot.
Place beef ball on skillet. Immediately smash flat with spatula. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook 2-3 min until edges are crispy and brown. Flip.
Add cheese immediately. Cook 1 more min.
Serve in lettuce wraps or buns with sliced tomato, pickles, and your choice of mustard, ketchup, or mayo.
recipes.tip: Use 80/20 beef for smash burgers - not leaner. The fat is what creates the lacy, crispy edges when smashed against a screaming hot surface. Leaner beef won't do this.
recipes.tip2: Use an 80/20 beef blend — the fat is essential. Leaner beef makes a dry, crumbly smash burger. The fat renders into the patty as it cooks and that is where the flavor lives.
recipe_detailed: Divide the ground beef into loose, rough balls — do not pack them tightly. About 3-4 oz each. Keep them cold until ready to cook.
Heat a cast iron skillet or griddle over the highest heat possible for 3-5 min until screaming hot. Add a thin layer of oil or butter.
Place a beef ball on the hot surface and immediately smash it flat with a spatula. Press hard — you want it thin, maybe a quarter inch. Season the top with salt and pepper.

Cook 2-3 min undisturbed until the edges look brown and lacy and the top is no longer pink. Flip once, add cheese immediately, and cook 30-60 more seconds. Build the burger on a toasted bun and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Smoked Ribs
recipes.desc: Slow-smoked baby back ribs with dry rub, served with coleslaw
recipe: Mix all dry rub spices. Remove membrane from back of ribs. Coat generously with rub.
Smoke at 225°F for 4-5 hours (or bake wrapped in foil at 275°F for 3 hours).
Unwrap last 30 min and brush with BBQ sauce.
Rest 10 min before cutting into individual ribs.
Toss coleslaw with vinegar, olive oil, salt. Serve alongside.
recipes.tip: The membrane on the back of the ribs must come off. Slide a butter knife under the corner, grab with a paper towel, and pull in one motion. It keeps the ribs from getting tough.
recipes.tip2: The 3-2-1 method: 3 hours smoke unwrapped, 2 hours wrapped in foil, 1 hour unwrapped with sauce to set the bark. The foil phase is what separates fall-off-bone from chewy.
recipe_detailed: Remove the membrane from the back of the ribs by sliding a butter knife under it and pulling with a paper towel for grip. This lets smoke and seasoning penetrate both sides.
Rub all surfaces generously with your seasoning blend. Let sit at room temperature 30 min, or refrigerate overnight for deeper flavor.
Set up your grill or smoker for indirect heat at 225-250F. Add wood chips. Place ribs bone-side down and smoke 3 hours.

Wrap tightly in foil with a splash of apple juice or butter inside. Cook wrapped 2 hours. Unwrap, brush with sauce, and cook 1 hour more. Ribs are done when the meat pulls back from the bone ends and a toothpick slides in with no resistance.

recipes.name: Lemon Herb Chicken Thighs
recipes.desc: Juicy bone-in thighs, roasted lemon, fresh herbs
recipe: Preheat oven to 425°F. Season chicken with rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Sear thighs skin-down 4 min until golden. Flip.
Add lemon slices and garlic. Roast 12-14 min.
Rest 3 min. Serve with mixed greens.
recipes.tip: Score the skin lightly with a sharp knife before searing. It renders the fat more evenly and gives you cracklier skin without curling.
recipes.tip2: Bone-in, skin-on thighs are much more forgiving than breasts — done between 165-185F and the fat keeps them moist even if you run a few minutes long. Internal temp is your best guide.
recipe_detailed: Pat chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels on all sides — dry skin crisps, wet skin steams. Season generously with salt, pepper, and herbs on both sides.

Heat an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add oil. Place thighs skin-side down and don't touch them for 7-8 min. They release when the skin is golden and crispy. Flip and cook 2 min on the other side.
Add garlic, lemon slices, and herbs to the pan. Transfer to a 400F oven and roast 18-22 min until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165F.
Let rest 5 min before serving. Spoon the pan juices over the chicken — they are the sauce.

recipes.name: Chicken Fajita Bowls
recipes.desc: Sizzled chicken strips, peppers & onions, avocado, lime crema
recipe: Season chicken with fajita seasoning.
Sear chicken 6-7 min. Set aside.
Cook peppers and onion 5 min until charred.
Mix yogurt with lime for crema. Build bowls.
recipes.tip: Don't move the chicken for the first 4 minutes. It will release naturally when the crust is ready - forcing it tears the skin and loses the sear.
recipes.tip2: Resting the chicken after cooking is what keeps it juicy. Cut too soon and all the juices run onto your cutting board instead of staying in the meat.
recipe_detailed: Slice chicken into strips and toss with fajita seasoning, oil, and lime juice. If you have time, marinate 15-30 min.

Heat a large cast iron skillet over high heat until very hot. Add chicken in a single layer — do not stir for 2 min, let it get a char on one side. Flip and cook 2 more min. Remove to a plate and rest.
In the same pan, add a little more oil and cook sliced peppers and onions over high heat 4-5 min until charred in spots, not just softened.
Slice the rested chicken and add back to the pepper mixture. Toss briefly. Serve over rice or in bowls with guac, sour cream, salsa, and warm tortillas.

recipes.name: Chicken & Veggie Sheet Pan
recipes.desc: Chicken thighs, broccoli, bell pepper, garlic, paprika
recipe: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss everything with oil and spices.
Arrange in single layer on sheet pan.
Roast 20-22 min, flipping veggies halfway.
Chicken should hit 165°F internal.
recipes.tip: Dry the chicken thighs completely with paper towels before seasoning. Surface moisture is the enemy of browning.
recipes.tip2: Denser vegetables like carrots and potatoes take longer than chicken. Give them a 10-min head start, or cut them smaller than softer veg so everything finishes at the same time.
recipe_detailed: Preheat oven to 425F. Line a large sheet pan with foil. Pat chicken dry and season with salt, pepper, and your seasoning blend.
Cut denser vegetables smaller than quick-cooking ones. Toss all vegetables in oil, salt, and pepper so each piece is lightly coated.
Spread vegetables on the pan in a single layer with space between pieces — crowding causes steaming, not roasting. Place chicken skin-side up on top of or between the vegetables.
Roast 25-35 min until the chicken reaches 165F and the vegetables are golden with some caramelized edges. Rotate the pan halfway through for even cooking.

recipes.name: Chicken Zoodle Soup
recipes.desc: Hearty broth, shredded chicken, zucchini noodles, carrots
recipe: Bring broth to simmer. Add carrots, celery, garlic.
Cook 8 min until almost tender.
Add chicken and thyme. Simmer 3 min.
Add zucchini noodles, cook 2 min. Season and serve topped with fresh parsley.
recipes.tip: Add the zucchini noodles in the last 90 seconds only. Overcooked zucchini releases water that dilutes your broth. Pull them while they still have bite.
recipes.tip2: Add zucchini noodles only at the very end — they need just 1-2 min and release water rapidly. Add them too early and they turn mushy and water down the broth.
recipe_detailed: Heat oil in a large pot over medium. Add onion, carrots, and celery and cook 5-6 min until softened. Add garlic, cook 1 min.
Add chicken broth and bring to a boil. Add chicken breasts or thighs whole — they poach gently and stay juicy. Reduce to a simmer and cook 15-18 min until cooked through.
Remove chicken and shred with two forks. Return shredded chicken to the pot. Add herbs and season well with salt and pepper. Taste the broth and adjust.
Add zucchini noodles and simmer 1-2 min until just softened. Serve immediately — don't let the soup sit with the zoodles or they turn to mush.

recipes.name: Coconut Curry Chicken
recipes.desc: Light coconut milk curry, chicken, spinach, jasmine rice
recipe: Sauté garlic and ginger 1 min. Add curry paste 1 min.
Add chicken, cook 5 min.
Pour in coconut milk and fish sauce. Simmer 8 min.
Stir in spinach and lime. Serve over steamed jasmine rice, topped with cilantro.
recipes.tip: Fry the curry paste in oil for a full minute until it darkens slightly and smells fragrant. This is called 'killing the paste' - raw paste tastes tinny.
recipes.tip2: Add spinach right at the end and remove the pan from heat. Residual warmth wilts it perfectly in 60 seconds — cooking it longer makes it slimy and dull.
recipe_detailed: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add garlic and ginger and cook 1 min, stirring, until fragrant but not browned. Add the curry paste and let it fry in the oil for a full minute, stirring constantly — it should darken slightly and smell toasty. This step is called blooming and it's what makes curry taste deep instead of flat.
Add the chicken pieces and cook 5–6 min, turning occasionally, until the outside is opaque and lightly golden. It doesn't need to be cooked through yet — it'll finish in the sauce.

Pour in the coconut milk and fish sauce. Stir to combine, scraping up any bits from the bottom. Bring to a gentle simmer (small bubbles, not a rolling boil) and cook 8 min. The chicken is done when it's no longer pink inside — cut the thickest piece to check.

Squeeze in the lime juice and stir in the spinach. Remove the pan from heat and let the residual warmth wilt the spinach for 60 seconds — it should turn bright green and just collapse. Serve over steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Chicken Bowls
recipes.desc: Teriyaki glazed chicken, edamame, cucumber, brown rice
recipe: Mix soy sauce, honey, vinegar, sesame oil for glaze.
Cook chicken 6-7 min per side. Add glaze last 2 min.
Slice chicken. Build bowls with rice, edamame, cucumber.
Top with sesame seeds.
recipes.tip: Pound the chicken to even thickness before cooking. Thick and thin spots cook at different rates - evening them out gets you perfect doneness edge to edge.
recipes.tip2: Homemade teriyaki is just soy sauce, mirin, and sugar reduced in a pan — it takes 3 min and is dramatically better than bottled. Make a double batch and keep it in the fridge.
recipe_detailed: For teriyaki sauce: combine soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and a little cornstarch in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves and it thickens slightly — about 3 min. Set aside.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high. Cook chicken skin-side down 5-6 min until deeply golden, then flip and cook 4 more min.
Pour the teriyaki sauce over the chicken and let it simmer and reduce 2-3 min, spooning it over the chicken as it thickens. It should be sticky and coat the back of a spoon.
Slice chicken and serve over steamed rice. Spoon extra sauce over everything. Top with sliced green onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Chicken Cauliflower Fried Rice
recipes.desc: Riced cauliflower, chicken, egg, peas, carrots, soy sauce
recipe: Heat oil in wok on high. Add jasmine rice, cook 3 min.
Push aside. Scramble eggs in center, mix together.
Add chicken, peas & carrots, garlic. Stir fry 3 min.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil. Top with green onion.
recipes.tip: The secret to fried rice is day-old cooked rice. Freshly cooked rice is too wet and clumps. If you don't have day-old, spread it on a sheet pan to cool and dry for 30 minutes.
recipes.tip2: Squeeze as much water out of the riced cauliflower as you can in a clean dish towel before cooking. Excess water makes it steam and clump. The drier it is, the more it mimics fried rice.
recipe_detailed: Pulse cauliflower in a food processor until it resembles rice. Spread on a towel and squeeze firmly to remove excess moisture — this step is critical for texture.
Season and cook chicken in a hot skillet with oil until cooked through, 6-8 min. Remove and dice into small pieces.

In the same pan over high heat, add sesame oil. Add garlic and ginger, stir 30 sec. Add cauliflower rice and stir fry 5 min — let it sit in contact with the pan for 30 seconds at a time to develop color.
Push everything to the sides. Scramble eggs in the center, then mix through. Add chicken, soy sauce, and any vegetables. Toss and cook 2 more min. Top with green onions.

recipes.name: One-Pan Chicken & Mushrooms
recipes.desc: Chicken thighs braised with mushrooms, thyme, dijon broth
recipe: Sear chicken 5 min per side. Remove.
Sauté mushrooms and garlic 4 min.
Whisk broth and dijon. Pour in, scrape pan.
Return chicken with thyme. Simmer 8 min. Top with parsley.
recipes.tip: After adding the dijon broth, scrape the fond (browned bits) from the bottom of the pan immediately. That's where the depth of flavor is stored.
recipes.tip2: Don't salt mushrooms at the start — it draws out water and they steam instead of brown. Cook them dry until the liquid evaporates, then season. That is when they start to brown.
recipe_detailed: Pat chicken dry and season all sides. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear chicken skin-side down 6-7 min without moving until deeply golden. Flip and cook 3 min. Remove to a plate.
Add mushrooms to the same pan in a single layer. Don't stir for 3 min — let them brown on one side. Toss and cook another 2 min. Now season with salt.
Add garlic and thyme and stir 1 min. Add broth and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pan, nestle into the sauce. Cover and cook over low heat 12-15 min until chicken reaches 165F. Stir in butter and cream if using, taste and adjust seasoning.

recipes.name: Chicken Shawarma Bowls
recipes.desc: Spiced chicken, romaine, tomato, tzatziki, tahini
recipe: Mix spices, garlic, oil. Coat chicken.
Sear 6-7 min per side.
Rest 3 min, then slice.
Build bowls with romaine and cherry tomatoes, then top with sliced chicken. Drizzle with tzatziki, tahini, and lemon.
recipes.tip: Marinate the chicken overnight if you can. Shawarma spices need time to penetrate - even 4 hours makes a noticeable difference in depth of flavor.
recipes.tip2: The longer the chicken marinates the better — the acid in lemon juice tenderizes the meat and the spices penetrate deeply. Even 30 min makes a difference; overnight is transformative.
recipe_detailed: Mix together all the shawarma spices with olive oil and lemon juice. Toss chicken thighs to coat completely. Marinate at least 30 min, up to overnight in the fridge.
Cook in a hot skillet over medium-high heat or under a broiler 5-7 min per side until cooked through and charred in spots. The spices should form a dark, fragrant crust.
Rest the chicken 5 min, then slice thin. While it rests, warm pita and prepare toppings: chopped cucumber, tomato, red onion, and parsley.
Build bowls: rice or pita base, sliced chicken, toppings, a generous drizzle of garlic sauce or tzatziki, and a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.name: Hot Wings
recipes.desc: Crispy baked wings, classic buffalo sauce, celery & blue cheese dip
ingredients: 4 lb chicken wings, split at joint
1/2 cup blue cheese or ranch dressing
recipe: Pat wings completely dry. Toss with baking powder, garlic powder, salt, pepper.
Arrange on wire rack over baking sheet. Refrigerate uncovered 1 hr (or overnight).
Bake at 425°F for 45-50 min, flipping halfway, until very crispy.
Melt butter, stir in hot sauce and Worcestershire for buffalo sauce.
Toss wings in sauce. Serve with celery and blue cheese or ranch.
recipes.tip: Baking powder on the wings draws out moisture and creates a porous surface that fries up incredibly crispy in the oven - it's the secret to oven wings that actually crunch.
recipes.tip2: The secret to crispy baked wings: baking powder in the coating. It raises the pH of the skin and makes it blister and crisp in the oven in a way plain flour cannot.
recipe_detailed: Pat wings completely dry — any moisture is the enemy of crispy skin. Toss with baking powder, salt, and pepper. No flour needed — the baking powder is the crispiness trick.
Arrange on a wire rack set over a foil-lined baking sheet. This lets hot air circulate under the wings. Bake at 425F for 45-50 min, flipping halfway, until deeply golden and the skin is blistered.
While wings bake, melt butter in a saucepan and whisk in hot sauce. Taste and adjust — more butter for mild, more sauce for hot.
Toss the hot wings immediately in the sauce so it clings while they are hot. Serve with blue cheese or ranch and celery sticks.

recipes.name: Blackened Chicken Greek Salad
recipes.desc: Cajun-spiced crispy chicken over romaine, feta, olives, cucumber, red onion, oregano dressing
ingredients: For dressing: 3 tbsp olive oil, 1.5 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp dried oregano, salt & pepper
recipe: Mix paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, thyme, salt, pepper. Coat chicken well on all sides.
Heat olive oil in cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Sear chicken 4-5 min per side until blackened and cooked through (165°F internal). Rest 3 min.
Whisk dressing ingredients together.
Build salad: romaine, tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, olives, feta.
Slice chicken and lay over salad. Drizzle dressing over everything.
recipes.tip: Cast iron is essential for proper blackening - you need sustained, intense heat that most pans can't hold. Get it smoking hot, add no oil to the pan, and don't touch the chicken.
recipes.tip2: Blackening is not burning — it is a controlled char from the spice crust. Use a cast iron over very high heat and don't be scared when it smokes. Open a window and let it happen.
recipe_detailed: Mix blackening spices: paprika, cayenne, garlic powder, thyme, oregano, salt, and pepper. Coat chicken on all sides — press the spices in gently.

Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat for 3-4 min until very hot. Add a thin film of oil. Add chicken and cook 4-5 min per side — it will smoke significantly and the crust will turn very dark. That is correct.
Rest the chicken 5 min then slice. While resting, assemble the salad: romaine, cucumber, tomatoes, Kalamata olives, red onion, pepperoncini, and crumbled feta.
Top the salad with sliced chicken and dress with olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and oregano. Serve with pita bread.

recipes.name: Zuppa Toscana
recipes.desc: Creamy Italian sausage soup with kale, potatoes, and a touch of cream
ingredients: 3 medium potatoes, thinly sliced or diced
2 cups heavy cream or coconut cream
recipe: Brown sausage in a large pot, breaking it up. Remove, leave drippings.
Sauté onion in drippings 4 min. Add garlic and red pepper flakes 1 min.
Add broth and potatoes. Bring to boil, simmer 10-12 min until potatoes are tender.
Return sausage. Stir in cream and kale.
Simmer 5 min until kale wilts. Season. Serve with parmesan.
recipes.tip: Don't drain all the drippings after browning the sausage , leave a thin layer. That's where the soup's depth of flavor lives.
recipes.tip2: Kale goes in last for a reason. Add it too early and it turns army-green and bitter. Those final 5 minutes give you bright, silky leaves.
recipe_detailed: Heat a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook 6-8 min, breaking it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon until no pink remains and the edges are starting to crisp. Use a slotted spoon to transfer to a plate , leave the drippings in the pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add the onion and cook 4-5 min, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent. Add garlic and red pepper flakes and stir 1 min , you'll smell them turn fragrant.
Pour in the broth and add the potatoes. Raise heat to bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook 10-12 min until a fork slides through a potato slice without resistance.
Return the sausage to the pot. Pour in the cream and add the kale. Stir to combine.
Simmer 4-5 min until the kale wilts and turns deep green. Taste and season with salt and pepper. Ladle into bowls and top generously with Parmesan.

recipes.name: Honey-Dijon Salmon Sheet Pan
recipes.desc: Glazed salmon, asparagus, lemon, roasted together
recipe: Preheat oven to 400°F. Mix honey, dijon, salt.
Place salmon and asparagus on sheet pan. Brush salmon with glaze.
Add lemon slices. Roast 14-16 min.
recipes.tip: Bring salmon to room temperature 15 minutes before cooking. Cold fish from the fridge cooks unevenly and often sticks to the pan.
recipes.tip2: The salmon is done when it flakes easily with a fork at the thickest part and has turned from translucent to opaque. It should still look slightly darker in the very center — that's perfect. If it's completely uniform it's overdone.
recipe_detailed: Take the salmon out of the fridge 15 min before cooking so it comes closer to room temperature — this helps it cook evenly. Preheat your oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with foil for easy cleanup.
In a small bowl, mix honey, dijon mustard, salt, and a crack of pepper. Taste it — it should be balanced, slightly sweet and tangy.

Place salmon fillets skin-side down on one side of the sheet pan and asparagus on the other. Spoon or brush the glaze generously over the top of each salmon fillet. Lay lemon slices over the asparagus and a couple on the salmon.

Roast 14–16 min. The salmon is done when it flakes easily with a fork at the thickest part and has turned from translucent to opaque — it should still look slightly darker in the very center. The asparagus should be tender with slightly charred tips.

recipes.name: Teriyaki Salmon & Broccoli
recipes.desc: Teriyaki glazed salmon, steamed broccoli, sesame seeds
recipe: Mix soy sauce, honey, vinegar, sesame oil for glaze.
Sear salmon 3 min, flip. Pour glaze over, cook 3 min more.
Steam broccoli 4 min.
Serve with remaining glaze, sesame seeds, green onion.
recipes.tip: Apply the teriyaki glaze in the last 2-3 minutes only. Sugar burns quickly - glazing too early results in bitterness instead of caramelization.
recipes.tip2: Salmon goes from perfect to dry fast. The center should still look slightly translucent when you pull it — it finishes cooking from residual heat as it rests. Uniformly opaque all the way through means overdone.
recipe_detailed: Pat salmon dry and season with salt and pepper. Make teriyaki sauce: whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and a little cornstarch. Bring to a simmer in a small pan 2-3 min until slightly thickened.
Heat oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high. Place salmon skin-side up and cook 3 min undisturbed to build a crust. Flip to skin-side down.

Brush teriyaki sauce over the salmon. Add broccoli florets around the pan with a splash of water. Cover and cook 4-5 min until broccoli is bright green and salmon flakes at the edges but looks slightly darker in the center.
Serve over steamed rice with extra sauce and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Salmon Patties & Coleslaw
recipes.desc: Canned salmon patties, tangy coleslaw, lemon-dill yogurt sauce
recipe: Mix salmon, egg, almond flour, dijon. Form patties.
Pan-fry in olive oil 3-4 min per side until golden.
Toss coleslaw with vinegar and salt.
Mix yogurt, dill, lemon juice for sauce. Serve everything together.
recipes.tip: Refrigerate the formed salmon patties for 15 minutes before frying. Chilling helps them hold together and prevents crumbling in the pan.
recipes.tip2: Chill the formed patties in the fridge for 15 min before frying — the binders set up and the patties hold together much better when they have had time to firm up.
recipe_detailed: Drain canned salmon thoroughly and pick out any bones. In a bowl, flake the salmon and mix with egg, breadcrumbs, diced onion, mustard, lemon juice, and seasoning. Don't overmix — just combine.
Form into patties about 3/4-inch thick. Place on a plate, cover, and refrigerate 15 min. This helps them hold together when frying.
Meanwhile, make coleslaw: shred cabbage and carrot, toss with mayo, vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper. Taste and adjust — it should be tangy and creamy.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high. Cook patties 3-4 min per side until golden brown. Serve with coleslaw on the side or on a bun.

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Salmon
recipes.desc: Pan-seared salmon, garlic butter sauce, crispy green beans
recipe: Season salmon with salt and pepper.
Sear skin-up in hot skillet 4 min per side. Remove.
Add butter and garlic. Cook 1 min.
Add green beans, toss 3 min. Return salmon, add lemon, parsley.
recipes.tip: Tilt the pan and baste the salmon repeatedly with the garlic butter in the last minute. This is called arroser - it infuses flavor into every layer of the fish.
recipes.tip2: Baste constantly in the last 2 minutes — spoon the hot garlic butter over the top of the salmon repeatedly. This bastes the top without needing to flip and creates incredible flavor.
recipe_detailed: Pat salmon dry. Season generously. Heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high until shimmering.
Place salmon skin-side up. Cook 4 min without moving — a proper crust should form. Flip to skin-side down.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter and garlic to the pan. As the butter melts and foams, continuously spoon it over the top of the salmon for 2-3 min. The salmon is done when it flakes easily at the thickest part and the center is slightly darker.
Add lemon juice to the butter in the pan, stir, and pour over the salmon. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.name: Salmon Taco Bowls
recipes.desc: Spiced salmon, cabbage slaw, avocado, mango salsa, chipotle lime crema
ingredients: 1 can (7 oz) chipotles in adobo sauce
Optional: chopped chipotles from can for topping
recipe: Make chipotle lime crema: whisk sour cream with 1-2 tbsp adobo sauce from the can and Tajin seasoning. Taste and adjust — should be smoky, tangy, and lightly spicy. Optionally chop a chipotle pepper and stir it in for more heat.
Season salmon with chili powder, cumin, salt. Pan-sear 4 min per side until cooked through. Flake into large chunks.
Quick slaw: toss cabbage with lime juice and a pinch of salt. Let sit 5 min.
Build bowls: slaw base, salmon chunks, avocado slices. Drizzle generously with crema. Add chopped chipotles on top if desired. Finish with fresh cilantro and lime.
recipes.tip: For the best slaw, squeeze the lime over the cabbage and let it sit 10 minutes before serving. The acid gently wilts the cabbage so it's tender but still has crunch.
recipes.tip2: For the avocado crema, blend avocado with lime juice, a little garlic, and sour cream until smooth. The lime juice prevents browning and the crema keeps in the fridge for 2 days — make extra.
recipe_detailed: Season salmon with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and a drizzle of oil. Cook in a hot skillet 3-4 min per side until cooked through with a slight char. Break into large chunks.
Warm corn tortillas or cook rice for bowl base. Shred purple cabbage and toss with lime juice and a pinch of salt.

Make chipotle lime crema first so it can chill: whisk sour cream with 1-2 tbsp of the adobo sauce from the can (that thick, smoky liquid, not just the peppers) and Tajin seasoning. Taste — it should be smoky, tangy, and lightly spicy. Stir in a squeeze of lime. Want more heat? Chop a chipotle pepper from the can and mix it in.
Assemble: base, salmon chunks, slaw, diced mango or pico de gallo, crema, and pickled jalapenos. Finish with fresh cilantro and lime wedges.

recipes.name: Black Bean Tacos
recipes.desc: Spiced black beans, corn tortillas, avocado, pickled onion, cilantro
recipe: Quick-pickle onion in lime juice and salt 10 min.
Heat beans with cumin, chili powder, salt. Mash slightly.
Warm tortillas in dry skillet.
Fill with beans, avocado, pickled onion, cilantro, salsa.
recipes.tip: Quick-pickle the onions for at least 15 minutes - longer is better. The lime juice turns them bright pink and mellows their raw sharpness into something sweet and tangy.

recipes.name: Chickpea Tikka Masala
recipes.desc: Chickpeas in rich tomato-spiced sauce, spinach, jasmine rice
recipe: Sauté onion until golden, 5 min. Add garlic and ginger 1 min.
Add tikka masala spice, toast 30 sec.
Add tomatoes and chickpeas. Simmer 10 min.
Stir in coconut milk and spinach. Serve over cauliflower rice, topped with fresh cilantro.
recipes.tip: Add a small pinch of sugar to the tikka sauce. It balances the acidity of the tomatoes and rounds out the spice blend without making it sweet.
recipes.tip2: Toast the spices dry for 30 seconds before adding liquid. You'll know they're ready when the kitchen smells incredible — that's the volatile oils releasing. Don't walk away during this step, they burn fast.
recipe_detailed: Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5–6 min, stirring occasionally, until golden and soft — not just translucent, you want some color here. It builds sweetness.

Add garlic and ginger and stir 1 min until fragrant. Add the tikka masala spice blend and toast it in the oil for 30 seconds, stirring constantly. The kitchen should smell incredible. Don't walk away — spices burn fast and turn bitter.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes and add the chickpeas. Stir to combine and bring to a simmer. Add a small pinch of sugar. Cook 10 min, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the color deepens to a rich orange-red.
Stir in coconut milk and spinach. Cook 2–3 min until the spinach wilts and the sauce is creamy and uniform. Taste and adjust salt. Serve over basmati rice with naan for scooping.

recipes.name: Lentil Veggie Soup
recipes.desc: Red lentils, kale, carrots, tomatoes, cumin-turmeric broth
recipe: Sauté onion and carrots 5 min. Add garlic and spices 1 min.
Add lentils, tomatoes, broth. Bring to boil.
Simmer 15 min until lentils are soft.
Stir in kale 3 min. Season and squeeze lemon over top.
recipes.tip: Red lentils break down completely as they cook, naturally thickening the soup. If it gets too thick, thin with a splash of water - don't add more broth, which concentrates salt.
recipes.tip2: Red lentils dissolve completely as they cook — that is by design. They are the thickener. Green or brown lentils hold their shape if you prefer texture; just add 10 more min of simmering.
recipe_detailed: Heat oil in a large pot over medium. Cook onion, carrot, and celery 5-6 min until softened. Add garlic, cook 1 min.
Add cumin, coriander, and smoked paprika. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add diced tomatoes, lentils, and broth. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook 20-25 min, stirring occasionally, until lentils are completely soft and have dissolved into the broth, thickening it.
Add any leafy greens and stir until wilted. Squeeze lemon juice in at the end — it brightens the whole soup. Season with salt and pepper.

recipes.name: Three Bean Chili
recipes.desc: Black, kidney & pinto beans, tomatoes, peppers, chili spices
recipe: Sauté onion and peppers 5 min. Add garlic and spices 1 min.
Add all beans (drained), tomatoes, tomato sauce.
Simmer 15 min, stirring occasionally.
Season. Serve with avocado, sour cream, cilantro.
recipes.tip: Let the chili sit for 15 minutes off heat before serving. Like any braise, resting allows the flavors to settle and meld - it genuinely tastes better.
recipes.tip2: Don't rush the spices — add them to the hot fat and stir for a full 30-60 seconds before adding liquid. This blooms them in oil, releasing the volatile flavor compounds that make chili taste complex instead of flat.
recipe_detailed: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high. Cook onion and peppers 5-6 min until softened. Add garlic, cook 1 min.
Add all the spices: chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, and cayenne. Stir for 30-60 seconds in the hot oil until intensely fragrant.
Add drained beans, crushed tomatoes, and broth. Stir well. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.

Simmer uncovered 25-30 min, stirring occasionally, until the chili thickens and the flavors meld. Taste and adjust seasoning — chili often needs more salt and sometimes a splash of vinegar at the end. Serve with sour cream, shredded cheese, and warm cornbread.

recipes.name: Plant-Based Taco Bowls
recipes.desc: Plant-based ground, black beans, salsa, avocado, romaine
recipe: Cook plant-based ground 5 min, breaking up.
Add taco seasoning + 2 tbsp water, stir 1 min.
Warm beans separately.
Build bowls: romaine, ground, beans, avocado, salsa, lime.
recipes.tip: Cook plant-based meat on high heat without stirring for the first 2 minutes. It needs to develop a crust just like real beef, and won't if you stir constantly.
recipes.tip2: Season the base heavily — whether it is lentils, cauliflower, or a blend, it needs to taste like taco meat on its own before it goes in the bowl. Bland filling makes a bland bowl.
recipe_detailed: Cook your taco base: for lentils, simmer in broth with taco seasoning 20 min until soft. For cauliflower, roast at 425F with taco spices 20 min until caramelized. Season aggressively — it should taste boldly spiced on its own.
Warm black or pinto beans in a pan with cumin, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt. Smash a few beans for a creamier texture.
Cook rice and season with lime juice and fresh cilantro.
Build bowls: rice base, beans, taco filling, salsa, guacamole, shredded cabbage, pickled jalapenos, and sour cream or cashew cream. Squeeze lime over everything.

recipes.name: Lasagna with Salad
recipes.desc: Hearty layered lasagna with mild Italian sausage, ricotta, mozzarella, and a crisp side salad
ingredients: 1.5 lb mild Italian sausage, casings removed
For salad: romaine, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, Italian dressing
recipe: Preheat oven to 375°F. Brown beef with garlic, drain. Mix in marinara.
Cook noodles al dente. Drain.
Mix ricotta, egg, half the parmesan, Italian seasoning.
Layer in 9x13 pan: sauce, noodles, ricotta, beef, mozzarella. Repeat.
Top with remaining mozzarella and parmesan. Cover with foil.
Bake 45 min. Remove foil, bake 15 more min until bubbly. Rest 10 min before cutting.
Toss salad and serve alongside.
recipes.tip: Rest the lasagna 15 minutes after pulling from the oven before cutting. The layers set during this time. Cutting immediately gives you a puddle; resting gives you clean squares.
recipes.tip2: Let the baked lasagna rest 20 min before cutting. The layers need time to set so they don't collapse when sliced. Fresh-from-the-oven lasagna is molten and falls apart — rested lasagna holds in perfect squares.
recipe_detailed: Make meat or vegetable sauce: brown protein or saute vegetables, add crushed tomatoes and herbs, and simmer 20 min until thick. Season well.
Make bechamel: melt butter, whisk in flour, cook 1 min, then gradually whisk in warm milk. Stir constantly until thick. Season with salt, nutmeg, and pepper.
Layer in a baking dish: sauce, lasagna sheets, bechamel, ricotta mixture if using, cheese. Repeat. Finish with bechamel and a generous layer of mozzarella and Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake at 375F for 40 min. Remove foil and bake 20 more min until bubbling and golden. Rest 20 min before cutting.

recipes.name: Homemade Pizza Night
recipes.desc: Make-your-own pizza with your choice of toppings - everyone builds their own
ingredients: Toppings of choice: pepperoni, bell peppers, onion, mushrooms, olives
recipe: Preheat oven to 475°F with a baking stone or sheet inside (gets it very hot).
Stretch or roll dough on a floured surface.
Brush with olive oil. Spread sauce, leaving 1" border.
Add cheese and toppings.
Bake directly on hot stone/pan 10-12 min until crust is golden and cheese is bubbling.
Top with fresh basil before serving.
recipes.tip: The hottest oven and hottest surface wins for pizza. Preheat your stone or pan inside the oven for 30 minutes. The immediate bottom heat is what creates a crispy base.
recipes.tip2: Preheat your oven as high as it goes for at least 45 min with a pizza stone or inverted baking sheet inside. The burst of intense heat from the hot surface is what creates the blistered, crispy bottom that a cold pan never achieves.
recipe_detailed: Make or use store-bought dough. Let dough rest at room temperature for 1 hour before stretching — cold dough is elastic and snaps back.
Stretch dough by hand on a lightly floured surface — don't use a rolling pin, it presses out the air bubbles that create airy crust. Work from the center outward.
Spread sauce very thinly — more sauce makes a soggy pizza. Add toppings, keeping cheese as the final layer. Don't overload.
Slide onto the preheated stone or pan and bake at the oven's highest setting 8-12 min until the crust is spotted with char and the cheese is bubbly and beginning to brown.

recipes.name: Chicken Piccata
recipes.desc: Pan-seared chicken in lemon-caper butter sauce, served with zucchini noodles
recipe: Dredge chicken in almond flour, salt, pepper.
Sear in olive oil 4 min per side. Remove.
Add garlic, broth, lemon juice to pan. Simmer 2 min.
Add butter and capers. Return chicken, spoon sauce over.
Serve over zucchini noodles with parsley.
recipes.tip: Pound the chicken between plastic wrap to a uniform quarter-inch thickness. Piccata needs thin, even cutlets - thick spots won't cook through by the time the crust is golden.
recipes.tip2: The butter goes in last and off the heat. This is called mounting — swirling cold butter into a hot sauce to emulsify it and give it a glossy, velvety texture. If the pan is too hot, the butter breaks and turns greasy.
recipe_detailed: Pound chicken breasts to an even half-inch thickness. Season with salt and pepper, then dredge in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil and butter in a skillet over medium-high until butter is foamy. Add chicken and cook 3-4 min per side until golden and cooked through. Remove to a plate.
In the same pan, add garlic and cook 30 seconds. Add white wine and lemon juice, scraping up any browned bits. Let it reduce by half, about 2 min.
Add capers and chicken broth. Simmer 2 min. Remove pan from heat and swirl in cold butter until the sauce is glossy and emulsified. Pour over chicken and top with fresh parsley.

recipes.name: Chicken Marsala & Risotto
recipes.desc: Golden chicken cutlets in a rich mushroom-Marsala wine sauce, served alongside a classic parmesan risotto
ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, pounded to 1/2 inch
8 oz cremini or baby bella mushrooms, sliced
recipe: Start risotto first: melt butter in a wide pan over medium. Sauté shallot until soft, 3 min. Add Arborio, stir to coat, toast 1 min. Add white wine, stir until absorbed.

Add warm broth to risotto one ladle at a time, stirring frequently, letting each addition absorb before adding the next. This takes 18-20 min. Finish with parmesan, season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.
While risotto cooks, season chicken and dredge in flour, shaking off excess. The flour coating is what gives the sauce its body.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear chicken 4-5 min per side until golden and cooked through (165°F). Do not move it while searing. Remove and rest on a plate.
In the same pan, melt 1 tbsp butter. Add mushrooms, cook undisturbed 3-4 min until golden. Add garlic 1 min. Pour in Marsala , it will sizzle dramatically. Scrape up any browned bits.
Add chicken broth and reduce sauce by half, about 3 min. Swirl in remaining butter and cream. Return chicken to pan, coat in sauce, simmer 2 min. Finish with parsley. Serve alongside risotto.
recipes.tip: Never stir risotto constantly , stir frequently but let it rest between additions. Constant stirring overworks the starch and makes it gluey. Use dry Marsala not sweet , sweet makes the sauce cloying.
recipes.tip2: For risotto, warm the broth before adding it. Cold broth shocks the rice and breaks the starchy creaminess you are building. Keep it in a pot on the adjacent burner on low the whole time.
recipe_detailed: Pound chicken to even thickness, dredge in flour. Sear in hot oil 3-4 min per side until golden. Remove to a plate.
In the same pan, cook mushrooms 5 min until browned. Add Marsala wine and let it bubble and reduce by half — about 3 min. Add broth, simmer 3 min. Swirl in butter. Return chicken to the pan.

For risotto: saute shallot in butter until soft. Add arborio rice and stir 1 min until translucent at the edges. Add wine, stir until absorbed. Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting until each addition is absorbed — about 20 min. Finish with butter and Parmesan.
Serve the chicken and Marsala sauce over the creamy risotto.

recipes.name: Chicken Enchilada Bowl
recipes.desc: Shredded chicken, enchilada sauce, black beans, peppers, jasmine rice
recipe: Warm chicken in enchilada sauce over medium heat, 5 min.
Sauté peppers in olive oil until tender.
Cook jasmine rice per package instructions.
Build bowls: cauli rice, peppers, beans, chicken.
Top with cheese, sour cream, cilantro, and lime.
recipes.tip: Char the bell peppers until slightly blackened before adding to the bowl. The smoky edges add complexity that makes the bowl taste slow-cooked rather than assembled.
recipes.tip2: Toast the dried chiles briefly in a dry skillet before making the sauce — 30 seconds per side until they puff and become fragrant. It unlocks a deeper, more complex flavor than untoasted chiles.
recipe_detailed: Season and cook chicken thighs in oil 6-7 min per side until cooked through and golden. Rest 5 min, then shred with two forks.
In the same pan, build the enchilada sauce: saute onion and garlic, add chili powder, cumin, and oregano, then crushed tomatoes and broth. Simmer 10 min. Blend if you want it smooth.
Toss shredded chicken with half the sauce. Build bowls: cilantro rice base, sauced chicken, pinto or black beans, and a ladle of extra sauce over the top.
Top with shredded cheese, sour cream, avocado, pickled jalapenos, and fresh cilantro.

recipes.name: Garlic Herb Roasted Chicken
recipes.desc: Crispy-skinned thighs roasted with garlic, rosemary, and lemon over vegetables
recipe: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss potatoes and green beans with oil and salt.
Season chicken with paprika, salt, pepper.
Nestle chicken among vegetables. Add garlic and lemon.
Roast 25-30 min until skin is crispy and chicken hits 165°F.
Rest 5 min before serving.
recipes.tip: Start the chicken skin-side down in a cold pan and bring the heat up gradually. This renders the fat slowly for the crispiest skin without burning.
recipes.tip2: Roast the chicken breast-side up the whole time. Flipping risks tearing the skin. Instead, rotate the pan halfway through for even browning. The high heat is what crisps the skin.
recipe_detailed: Pat the whole chicken dry inside and out — the most important step for crispy skin. Mix softened butter with garlic, herbs, salt, and pepper. Carefully loosen the skin over the breasts and rub butter directly onto the meat under the skin. Rub the rest all over the outside.
Truss the legs together with kitchen twine and tuck the wing tips under. Season the cavity with salt and stuff with lemon halves and fresh herbs.
Roast breast-side up at 425F for 60-80 min depending on size. The chicken is done when a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165F and the juices run clear.
Let the chicken rest 10-15 min before carving — the juices redistribute as it rests. Carve and serve with pan drippings spooned over.

recipes.name: Thai Basil Chicken
recipes.desc: Spicy ground chicken stir-fry with basil, fish sauce, and Thai chilies over rice
recipe: Heat oil in wok on high. Add garlic and chilies, 30 sec.
Add chicken, cook until no longer pink, 5 min.
Add fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, honey. Toss 1 min.
Remove from heat, fold in basil.
Serve over steamed jasmine rice, top with a fried egg if desired.
recipes.tip: Thai basil is not the same as regular basil - don't substitute. Thai basil has a slightly anise-like flavor that makes this dish authentic. It's usually in the Asian section.
recipes.tip2: Add the basil at the very end and off the heat — high heat destroys the volatile oils that give Thai basil its anise-like flavor. Thirty seconds of residual heat is all it needs to wilt beautifully.
recipe_detailed: Mince or finely chop the chicken or use ground chicken. Prepare all aromatics before you start — Thai basil chicken cooks in about 5 min total.
Heat oil in a wok over very high heat. Add garlic and Thai chilis and stir fry 30 seconds. Add chicken and stir fry 3-4 min, breaking up any clumps, until cooked through and starting to crisp.
Add oyster sauce, fish sauce, and soy sauce. Toss to coat for 1 min. Remove from heat.
Add fresh Thai basil leaves and toss — residual heat wilts them in 30 seconds. Serve over jasmine rice, topped with a crispy fried egg if desired.

recipes.name: Chicken Souvlaki Bowls
recipes.desc: Grilled marinated chicken over greens with tzatziki, cucumber, and tomato
recipe: Marinate chicken in oil, lemon, garlic, oregano, cumin, salt 15 min.
Cook in hot skillet or on grill 6-8 min turning.
Assemble bowls: romaine, cucumber, tomato.
Top with chicken and drizzle tzatziki generously.
recipes.tip: Soak wooden skewers 30 minutes before grilling. Dry skewers ignite and burn, making the food taste acrid. Or use metal skewers and skip the step entirely.
recipes.tip2: If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 30 min first so they do not catch fire on the grill. Metal skewers conduct heat and cook the chicken from the inside out — slightly faster.
recipe_detailed: Cut chicken into 1.5-inch cubes. Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Marinate at least 30 min.
Thread onto skewers, leaving a little space between pieces so they cook evenly.
Grill or cook in a hot grill pan 10-12 min, turning every few minutes, until cooked through with char marks.

Make tzatziki while the chicken cooks: stir together Greek yogurt, grated cucumber squeezed dry, garlic, dill, lemon juice, and salt. Serve chicken over rice or in pita with tzatziki, tomatoes, red onion, and Kalamata olives.

recipes.name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
recipes.desc: Pan chicken in a sun-dried tomato, spinach, and cream sauce
recipe: Season and sear chicken 5-6 min per side. Remove.
Sauté garlic 1 min. Add sun-dried tomatoes.
Pour in broth and cream. Add Italian seasoning. Simmer 3 min.
Stir in parmesan and spinach until wilted.
Return chicken, spoon sauce over.
recipes.tip: Sun-dried tomatoes in oil are better here than dry-packed. The oil carries flavor and helps the sauce emulsify into something silky rather than broken.
recipes.tip2: When you add cream to a hot pan, reduce the heat to medium-low. Cream scorches quickly over high heat and a broken sauce is hard to rescue.
recipe_detailed: Pat chicken thighs dry and season. Sear in a hot oven-safe skillet 5-6 min per side until golden. Remove to a plate.
In the same pan over medium, saute garlic 1 min. Add sun-dried tomatoes and cook 1 min. Add spinach and stir until wilted.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Pour in heavy cream and chicken broth. Stir to combine and bring to a gentle simmer. Add Parmesan and stir until melted and the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Return chicken to the pan, spoon sauce over, and simmer 5 min until heated through. Taste and season. Serve over pasta or with crusty bread.

recipes.name: Honey Garlic Chicken Thighs
recipes.desc: Sticky honey-garlic glazed chicken thighs, broccoli, brown rice
recipe: Mix honey, soy, garlic, vinegar for glaze.
Sear chicken 5-6 min per side. Drain excess fat.
Pour glaze in pan, cook 2 min until sticky.
Steam broccoli 4 min.
Serve over rice with broccoli, sesame seeds, green onion.
recipes.tip: Don't add the glaze until the last 90 seconds. Honey burns fast. Let the chicken cook almost entirely through first, then glaze and let it caramelize just before resting.
recipes.tip2: Watch the honey garlic sauce closely in the final minute — the sugar in honey burns fast. You want it thick and sticky, not burnt and bitter. Pull the pan off if it starts smoking.
recipe_detailed: Pat chicken thighs dry and season with salt and pepper. Mix honey, soy sauce, and minced garlic in a small bowl.
Heat oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high. Sear thighs skin-side down 6-7 min until the skin is deeply golden and releases naturally. Flip and cook 3 min.
Pour the honey garlic glaze over the chicken. Let it bubble and reduce 1-2 min, spooning it over the chicken as it thickens. Watch it carefully — honey burns quickly.
Transfer to a 400F oven for 8-10 min until the chicken reaches 165F and the glaze is sticky and caramelized. Rest 3 min before serving.

recipes.name: Beef Bulgogi Bowls
recipes.desc: Korean marinated beef, sesame, cucumber, kimchi over jasmine rice
recipe: Mix soy, sesame oil, honey, garlic, ginger, pear. Marinate beef 10+ min.
Cook beef in hot skillet in batches, 2-3 min. Don't overcrowd.
Cook jasmine rice per package instructions.
Build bowls: rice, beef, cucumber, kimchi.
Top with sesame seeds and green onion.
recipes.tip: Grated Asian pear is a traditional tenderizer in bulgogi marinades - it contains enzymes that break down muscle fibers. Even 30 minutes makes the beef noticeably more tender.
recipes.tip2: Asian pear or kiwi in the bulgogi marinade is not just for flavor — the natural enzymes tenderize the beef fibers as it sits. Even 30 min with pear makes a noticeable difference in texture.
recipe_detailed: Slice beef ribeye or sirloin paper-thin against the grain. If it is hard to slice thin, freeze for 20 min first.
Mix marinade: soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, grated Asian pear or kiwi, garlic, ginger, and black pepper. Toss beef in marinade and refrigerate at least 30 min, preferably 2 hours.
Cook in a very hot pan or grill pan in batches — don't crowd or it steams. Sear 1-2 min per side until caramelized at the edges and cooked through.
Serve over rice with stir-fried vegetables, kimchi, sliced green onion, and sesame seeds. A fried egg on top is traditional.

recipes.name: Carne Guisada
recipes.desc: Tender Mexican beef stew with peppers, tomatoes, and cumin gravy
ingredients: Tortillas or cauli rice to serve
recipe: Brown beef in batches in olive oil. Remove.
Sauté onion, jalapeño, garlic 4 min. Add spices 1 min.
Add tomatoes and broth. Return beef.
Simmer covered 30-35 min until tender.
Serve with warm tortillas or over cilantro-lime rice.
recipes.tip: Cut the beef chuck into larger cubes than you think - 2 inches. Small pieces overcook and dry out during the braise. Large pieces break down properly and stay moist.
recipes.tip2: Don't rush the browning step — deeply searing the beef on all sides builds a fond on the bottom of the pot that becomes the flavor base of the entire stew. Pale grey beef makes a pale grey stew.
recipe_detailed: Cut beef chuck into 1.5-inch cubes. Pat dry and season generously. Brown in batches in a heavy pot over high heat until deeply seared on all sides — do not crowd the pan. Remove each batch.
In the same pot, saute onion, bell pepper, and garlic until softened. Add cumin, chili powder, and oregano, stir 1 min.
Add diced tomatoes, broth, and return the beef. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a very low simmer.
Braise covered 1.5-2 hours until the beef is fall-apart tender. Stir in a spoonful of masa harina dissolved in water to thicken. Serve with warm flour tortillas and rice.

recipes.name: Beef Fajita Bowls
recipes.desc: Sizzled skirt steak, charred peppers and onions, avocado, lime
recipe: Season steak with fajita seasoning.
Sear in hot skillet 2-3 min per side. Rest and slice.
In same pan, char peppers and onion 5 min.
Build bowls: cauli rice, steak, peppers, avocado.
Finish with lime, sour cream, and salsa.
recipes.tip: Sear the beef in a single layer without moving it for at least 3 minutes. Resist the urge to stir. The crust is where the flavor lives, and it won't form if the meat steams.
recipes.tip2: Marinate the steak in lime juice, oil, and cumin for at least 30 min but no more than 4 hours — beyond that, the acid starts to cook the surface of the meat and gives it an unpleasant mealy texture.
recipe_detailed: Slice flank steak thin against the grain. Toss with lime juice, oil, cumin, garlic powder, and chili powder. Marinate 30 min to 4 hours.
Cook in a screaming hot cast iron pan in batches — 1-2 min per side maximum. The goal is char, not thorough cooking. The thin slices cook through in seconds. Rest 3 min before serving.
In the same pan, cook sliced peppers and onion over high heat 4-5 min until charred at the edges.
Build bowls: rice or lettuce base, beef and peppers, guacamole, pico de gallo, sour cream, and shredded cheese. Squeeze lime over everything.

recipes.name: Birria-Style Beef Tacos
recipes.desc: Braised chili-spiced beef, crispy fried tacos, consommé for dipping
ingredients: White onion, cilantro, lime to serve
recipe: Blend soaked chiles, garlic, cumin, oregano, broth into sauce.
Brown beef, pour sauce over. Braise covered 45-50 min until shreddable.
Shred beef. Reserve braising liquid as consommé.
Dip tortillas in consommé, fill with beef and cheese, fry until crispy.
Serve with onion, cilantro, lime, and consommé for dipping.
recipes.tip: The consommé dip is not optional. It's what transforms birria tacos from good to extraordinary. Dip the assembled taco briefly - just enough to coat, not soak.
recipes.tip2: Dip the tortilla into the top of the consomme before frying — the fat that floats on top of the broth is where the color comes from. A properly dipped tortilla turns a deep, brilliant orange-red in the pan.
recipe_detailed: Make the adobo: toast dried guajillo and ancho chiles in a dry pan 30 seconds per side. Remove stems and seeds, soak in hot water 15 min. Blend with garlic, oregano, cumin, and some soaking liquid.
Season beef chunks generously. Brown in batches in a Dutch oven. Add the chile sauce and enough broth to cover. Braise at 325F for 3 hours until pull-apart tender. Shred beef into the broth.
Dip corn tortillas into the top of the consomme. Cook in a hot dry skillet 1-2 min per side until crispy. Fill with shredded beef and cheese, fold in half.
Serve with a small bowl of warm consomme for dipping. Top tacos with white onion, fresh cilantro, and lime.

recipes.name: Pork Carnitas Bowls
recipes.desc: Crispy shredded pork over greens with pico, avocado, and lime crema
recipe: Season pork. Cook in instant pot 25 min (or slow cooker 6-8 hrs) with OJ, lime, garlic.
Shred pork, spread on sheet pan, broil 3-4 min until crispy.
Mix yogurt with lime juice for crema.
Build bowls: romaine, carnitas, avocado, pico, crema.
recipes.tip: The broil step at the end is what makes carnitas. Without crisping the edges under high heat, you just have pulled pork. The caramelized bits are the whole point.
recipes.tip2: After the long braise, spread the pork on a sheet pan and broil it — 5 min is enough to caramelize the edges and create those crispy, charred bits that make carnitas special. Don't skip the broil.
recipe_detailed: Cut pork shoulder into large chunks, season generously with salt, pepper, cumin, oregano, and garlic. Place in a Dutch oven or slow cooker with orange juice, lime juice, and diced onion.
Braise in a 325F oven 3-4 hours or slow cook on low 8 hours until the pork shreds easily when pressed.
Remove pork, shred roughly with two forks. Spread on a foil-lined sheet pan. Pour some cooking liquid over the meat. Broil 5-7 min until edges crisp and caramelize — watch closely.
Serve in bowls over cilantro rice with black beans, pico de gallo, shredded cheese, sour cream, and avocado. Squeeze lime over everything.

recipes.name: Pork Tenderloin & Roasted Apples
recipes.desc: Herb-crusted pork tenderloin with caramelized apples and green beans
recipe: Preheat oven to 425°F. Rub tenderloin with oil, rosemary, thyme, garlic, salt.
Sear in oven-safe skillet 3 min per side.
Add apple slices and green beans around pork. Drizzle honey over apples.
Roast 14-16 min until pork hits 145°F. Rest 5 min.
Slice and serve with apples and green beans.
recipes.tip: Pull the pork from the oven at 145°F and rest 5 minutes. USDA guidelines allow medium doneness - well-done pork tenderloin is dry and chalky.
recipes.tip2: Pork tenderloin is very lean and overcooks fast. Pull it at 140-145F internal temp — it will look slightly pink in the center, which is safe and keeps it juicy. Cooking to 160F turns it grey and dry.
recipe_detailed: Pat pork tenderloin dry and season generously. Sear in a hot oven-safe skillet with oil over medium-high heat, turning to brown all sides, about 6 min total.
Remove pork. In the same pan, add apple wedges and onion slices. Cook 2-3 min until starting to soften. Add a splash of apple cider or broth to deglaze.
Return pork to the pan on top of the apple mixture. Transfer to a 400F oven for 15-20 min until a thermometer reads 140-145F.
Rest pork 5 min before slicing — the temperature will rise to 145F as it rests. Slice into medallions and serve with the pan apples and any juices.

recipes.name: Pork & Veggie Stir Fry
recipes.desc: Ground pork, snap peas, bok choy, ginger-garlic sauce over cauli rice
recipe: Brown pork in a wok over high heat. Drain fat.
Add garlic and ginger 1 min.
Add bok choy and snap peas, stir fry 3 min.
Add soy sauce, sesame oil, honey. Toss 1 min.
Serve over steamed jasmine rice with sesame seeds.
recipes.tip: Use medium-high heat and don't add the sauce until you've gotten good color on the vegetables. Sauce added too early steams everything and prevents browning.
recipes.tip2: Freeze the pork loin for 20 min before slicing — it firms up and you can cut it much thinner than fully thawed meat. Thin slices cook in 2 min and stay tender.
recipe_detailed: Slice pork thin against the grain. Toss with soy sauce, cornstarch, and a little sesame oil. Let sit 10 min.
Heat a wok over highest heat until smoking. Add oil, then pork in a single layer. Sear 60 seconds, toss, cook 30 more seconds. Remove — it should be just cooked through.
In the same wok, stir fry dense vegetables first 2 min, then softer ones 1 min. Add garlic and ginger.
Return pork. Add stir fry sauce. Toss everything 1 min until sauce thickens and coats. Serve over rice.

recipes.name: Pork Chops & Mushroom Gravy
recipes.desc: Pan-seared thick-cut pork chops in savory mushroom and herb gravy
recipe: Season pork chops well. Sear in hot skillet 4-5 min per side. Remove.
Sauté mushrooms 5 min. Add garlic and thyme 1 min.
Add broth and Worcestershire, scrape up bits. Simmer 3 min.
Swirl in butter, return chops, spoon gravy over. Serve.
recipes.tip: Resist the urge to move the pork chops while searing. They'll release naturally when a proper crust has formed. Forcing them early tears the crust and loses the fond.
recipes.tip2: Scraping up the browned bits (fond) when you add the broth is not optional — that's where the gravy's flavor is. Use a wooden spoon and really get in there.
recipe_detailed: Pat the pork chops completely dry with paper towels — moisture is the enemy of a good sear. Season generously on both sides with salt and pepper. Dry surface + hot pan = crust.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add the chops and don't touch them — let them sear 4–5 min. They'll release naturally when they've built a crust. Flip and sear the other side 3–4 min. They should be deep golden brown. Remove to a plate — they may not be fully cooked through yet and that's fine.
Reduce heat to medium. Add mushrooms to the same pan and cook 5 min without stirring much, letting them brown on one side before tossing. Add garlic and thyme and stir 1 min.
Pour in the broth and Worcestershire sauce. Use a wooden spoon to scrape up every bit of the browned residue from the bottom — that's concentrated flavor. Simmer 3 min until slightly reduced.

Swirl in the cold butter — this gives the gravy a glossy, velvety texture. Return the pork chops to the pan, spoon gravy generously over them, and let them rest in the sauce 2 min. The residual heat finishes cooking them through.

recipes.name: Sausage & Pepper Skillet
recipes.desc: Italian sausage, bell peppers, onions, marinara over zucchini noodles
recipe: Sear sausage slices until browned, 5 min. Remove.
Sauté peppers and onion 5 min. Add garlic 1 min.
Return sausage, add marinara and seasoning. Toss 2 min.
Sauté zucchini noodles 2 min separately.
Plate noodles, top with sausage mixture and parmesan.
recipes.tip: Brown the sausage in a dry pan with no added oil - there's plenty of fat in the sausage itself. Rendering its own fat creates better browning than oil ever could.
recipes.tip2: Brown the sausage slices in a single layer without stirring — those browned, caramelized cut faces are packed with flavor. Stirring constantly gives you grey sausage with no crust.
recipe_detailed: Slice sausage into rounds. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add sausage in a single layer cut-side down. Cook 3-4 min without stirring until deeply browned on one face. Flip and cook 2 min. Remove.
In the same pan, add sliced bell peppers and onion. Cook over medium-high heat 5-6 min until softened and charred at the edges — let them sit without stirring for 2 min at a time.
Add garlic, Italian seasoning, and crushed tomatoes if using. Stir and cook 2 min. Return sausage to the pan and toss everything together.
Serve over rice, pasta, or in hoagie rolls. Top with fresh basil.

recipes.name: Miso-Glazed Salmon
recipes.desc: Umami-rich miso and honey glazed salmon, edamame, cucumber, sesame
recipe: Mix miso, honey, soy, vinegar, sesame oil for glaze.
Coat salmon with glaze.
Bake at 400°F 10-12 min or broil 6-8 min until caramelized.
Warm edamame.
Build bowls: cucumber, edamame, salmon. Top with sesame seeds and green onion.
recipes.tip: White miso is mild and sweet. Red miso is more intense. Either works, but white gives you a more delicate glaze that pairs better with salmon without overpowering it.
recipes.tip2: Watch the miso glaze closely after the 5-minute mark — the sugars in miso and mirin burn fast and go from perfectly caramelized to bitter in under a minute.
recipe_detailed: Whisk together white miso paste, mirin, sake, and sugar until smooth. Spread generously over the salmon fillets. Marinate 30 min minimum — overnight makes it significantly better.
Preheat broiler to high. Line a baking sheet with foil and lightly oil it. Place salmon skin-side down.
Broil 6-8 min, watching closely after 5 min. The glaze should bubble and turn deep amber-brown in spots. The salmon is done when it flakes at the edges.
Serve over steamed rice with pickled ginger and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Coconut Lime Salmon Bowls
recipes.desc: Baked salmon with coconut-lime marinade, mango, avocado, cilantro
recipe: Mix coconut milk, lime juice, garlic, honey. Marinate salmon 10 min.
Bake at 400°F 12-14 min.
Toss cauli rice with lime zest and cilantro.
Build bowls: rice, salmon, mango, avocado.
Squeeze extra lime over everything.
recipes.tip: Line the baking dish with banana leaves or parchment before adding the marinated salmon. It prevents sticking and infuses a subtle grassy aroma into the fish.
recipes.tip2: Add the lime juice at the end of simmering, not the beginning. Long cooking makes lime bitter. A squeeze at the very end keeps it bright, fresh, and acidic.
recipe_detailed: Make the coconut lime broth: simmer coconut milk, a little broth, garlic, and ginger over medium heat 5 min.
Season salmon and nestle into the broth. Cover and poach gently over low heat 8-10 min until the salmon flakes easily. This gentle method keeps it incredibly moist.
Remove salmon. Squeeze lime juice into the broth, taste and season with salt.
Serve over jasmine rice. Ladle broth over the bowls, top with salmon, fresh cilantro, sliced green onion, and sliced chili.

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Shrimp & Asparagus
recipes.desc: Jumbo shrimp in garlic butter sauce with crispy roasted asparagus
ingredients: 1.5 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
recipe: Roast asparagus at 425°F with olive oil and salt for 10 min.
Heat butter in skillet. Add garlic and red pepper flakes 1 min.
Add shrimp in single layer. Cook 2 min per side until pink.
Squeeze lemon over. Top with parsley.
Plate asparagus and shrimp together.
recipes.tip: Pat the shrimp absolutely dry before seasoning. Wet shrimp steam instead of sear and will never develop color. A 2-minute pan-sear on dry shrimp beats 5 minutes on wet.
recipes.tip2: Shrimp overcook in seconds. Once they curl into a C-shape and turn pink, they are done. An O-shape means overcooked. When in doubt, pull them 30 seconds early — they keep cooking in residual heat.
recipe_detailed: Pat shrimp dry and season with salt, pepper, and paprika. Trim woody ends off asparagus.
Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add asparagus and cook 3-4 min, tossing occasionally, until bright green and just tender. Remove to a plate.

In the same pan, melt butter over medium-high. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add shrimp in a single layer and cook 1-2 min per side until they curl into a C-shape and turn pink throughout.
Return asparagus to the pan. Add a squeeze of lemon and toss everything together. Serve over rice or pasta.

recipes.name: Cajun Shrimp Bowls
recipes.desc: Spicy Cajun shrimp over jasmine rice with corn and avocado
ingredients: 1.5 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
recipe: Toss shrimp with Cajun seasoning.
Sear in hot skillet 2 min per side. Don't overcook.
Warm corn in same pan.
Build bowls: cauli rice, corn, shrimp, avocado.
Finish with lime juice and cilantro.
recipes.tip: Don't overcook the shrimp - pull them the instant they curl into a C shape and turn opaque. Overcooked shrimp are rubbery in seconds. They carry over from the residual heat.
recipes.tip2: Make the Cajun seasoning yourself: paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, thyme, oregano, salt, and pepper. Store-bought blends often have too much salt and not enough heat.
recipe_detailed: Toss shrimp with Cajun seasoning and a little oil so every shrimp is coated.

Heat a cast iron or heavy skillet over high heat until very hot. Add shrimp in a single layer — sear 1-2 min per side without stirring, until you see a slight char and they are cooked through. Work in batches if needed.
Cook rice according to package. Saute onion, pepper, and celery in the shrimp drippings for 3 min, then serve alongside.
Build bowls: rice, shrimp, corn, avocado, and black beans. Drizzle with remoulade or creamy Cajun sauce and top with green onions.

recipes.name: Shrimp Tacos
recipes.desc: Lime-marinated shrimp, cabbage slaw, avocado crema, corn tortillas
recipe: Season shrimp with cumin, chili powder, salt. Cook 2 min per side.
Toss cabbage with lime juice and salt.
Blend avocado with yogurt and lime for crema.
Warm tortillas. Build tacos: slaw, shrimp, crema, cilantro.
recipes.tip: Season the shrimp aggressively. They cook fast and briefly, so there's limited time for flavors to develop. Season more than you think is right.
